slides.narration: Welcome to CPY 701, Introduction to Counseling Psychology, a core course in the Master's degree in Counseling Psychology. I am glad you are here. This is week one of sixteen, and in this first lecture we ask the most fundamental question of all: what exactly is counseling psychology? By the end of this session you will be able to define the specialty, place it on the helping continuum, and describe the values, scope and limits that govern professional practice.

slides.title: What you will be able to do by the end of this week

items.text: counseling psychology from authoritative sources, in your own words.
guidance, counseling and psychotherapy without confusing them.
the core values of the specialty and its scope of practice, including where competence ends and referral begins.
the scientist-practitioner-advocate identity this programme expects you to grow into.

slides.narration: Here is what this week promises. First, you will define counseling psychology from authoritative sources. Second, you will distinguish guidance, counseling and psychotherapy without confusing them. Third, you will explain the core values of the specialty and its scope of practice, including where your competence ends and referral begins. And fourth, you will describe the scientist, practitioner and advocate identity that this programme expects you to grow into. Keep these four outcomes beside you as we move; every slide today serves one of them.

slides.title: Counseling psychology: a working picture

items.text: Governed by training, ethics and regulation, not by good intentions.
Works through mental processes, behaviour and relationship, not through medicine or coercion.
Its engine is a deliberate, boundaried relationship between a trained counselor and a client who seeks change.
It applies psychological theory, research and technique to help people improve wellbeing, resolve problems in living, and develop personally, socially, educationally and vocationally.

slides.narration: Let us begin with a working picture. Counseling psychology is a professional specialty within psychology. It applies psychological theory, research and technique to help people improve their wellbeing, resolve problems in living, and develop personally, socially, educationally and vocationally. Notice three things in that sentence. It is professional: it is governed by training, ethics and regulation, not by good intentions. It is psychological: it works through mental processes, behaviour and relationship, not through medicine or coercion. And it is helping: its engine is a deliberate, boundaried relationship between a trained counselor and a client who seeks change. Everything else in this course grows from those three anchors.

slides.title: Three definitions worth keeping

cards.title: APA Division 17
cards.text: A specialty that facilitates personal and interpersonal functioning across the lifespan: emotional, social, vocational, educational, health-related and developmental concerns.

cards.title: Corey (2021)
cards.text: A collaborative process between two people, in which the counselor's attitudes and skills help the client examine and change behaviour, thoughts and feelings.

cards.title: Gladding (2021)
cards.text: The professional practice of helping people who are not severely disturbed to solve problems, make decisions and grow.

slides.narration: Now let three authoritative voices sharpen the definition. The Society of Counseling Psychology, Division 17 of the American Psychological Association, describes the field as a specialty that facilitates personal and interpersonal functioning across the lifespan, focusing on emotional, social, vocational, educational, health-related and developmental concerns. Corey reminds us that counseling is a collaborative process between two people, in which the counselor's attitudes and skills help the client examine and change behaviour. Gladding calls counseling the professional practice of helping people who are not severely disturbed to solve problems and make decisions. Hear the common thread: ordinary people, real problems, a trained helper, and change that the client owns.

slides.quote: The curious paradox is that when I accept myself just as I am, then I can change.
slides.by: Carl R. Rogers · founder of person-centred counseling
slides.narration: Carl Rogers left us a line that captures the heart of our work: the curious paradox is that when I accept myself just as I am, then I can change. Counseling psychology is not about fixing broken people. It is about creating conditions in which a person, accepted and understood, can move toward their own potential. Hold that paradox; it will return in every theory we study.

slides.title: The helping continuum

nodes.title: Guidance
nodes.text: Informative, preventive, educational: information and direction for choices.

nodes.title: Counseling
nodes.text: Relational process with situational and developmental distress; ordinary functioning.

nodes.title: Psychotherapy
nodes.text: Longer, intensive work with entrenched personality and chronic emotional patterns.

nodes.title: Medical treatment
nodes.text: Diagnosis-led psychiatric care; medication and medical management.

slides.note: The boundaries blur in practice; the direction of travel, depth, duration and training differ.
slides.narration: Where does counseling sit on the helping road? Picture a continuum. At one end is guidance: informative, preventive and often educational, giving students or clients the information and direction they need, for example choosing a course or a career. Next is counseling: a deeper, relational process with clients who are experiencing adjustment, developmental or situational distress but remain within the range of ordinary functioning. Further along is psychotherapy: longer, more intensive work with deeper-seated personality or chronic emotional difficulties. And at the far end sits psychiatric and medical treatment, where diagnosis and medication lead. The boundaries blur in practice, but the direction of travel, depth, duration and training differ.

slides.title: Guidance, counseling and psychotherapy side by side
rows: Adjustment and developmental problems in living
Deeper personality and chronic emotional patterns
Students and groups, generally well adjusted
Individuals or couples in situational distress
Individuals with entrenched or diagnosed difficulties
Medium to long term: months or years
slides.note: The columns describe emphasis, not walls: real practice overlaps.
slides.narration: Let us make those differences concrete. Guidance is typically brief, informational and preventive; its client is often a student or a group; a teacher or guidance officer may deliver it. Counseling is relational and focused on present problems in living; its client is a person or couple in situational distress; the counselor holds postgraduate professional training. Psychotherapy runs longer, works with more entrenched patterns and often with diagnosed disorders; the psychotherapist or clinical psychologist leads it. Memorise the table's dimensions, focus, client, duration, depth and practitioner, because examination questions love to ask you to distinguish these three in practice.

slides.title: Counseling psychology among its neighbours

left.title: What we share
items: Psychological assessment and diagnostic awareness
Evidence-based intervention and outcome measurement
Ethics, confidentiality and informed consent
Work inside multidisciplinary teams and referral networks

right.title: What distinguishes us
items: Emphasis on strengths, resources and resilience
Developmental and vocational concerns taken as seriously as disorder
Prevention and brief, focal intervention
Culture, context and social justice treated as clinical facts
Normal-range distress addressed before it becomes pathology

slides.narration: A frequent confusion: how is counseling psychology different from clinical psychology and psychiatry? We share much: assessment, diagnostic awareness, evidence-based intervention, and ethics. What distinguishes us is emphasis. Counseling psychology stresses strengths and resources, not only pathology; it works with developmental and vocational concerns as seriously as with disorder; it favours brief, focal, preventive intervention; and it treats culture, context and social justice as clinical facts, not footnotes. Psychiatry adds medical training and prescribing; clinical psychology leans harder on severe psychopathology and assessment batteries. Knowing the overlap protects you from turf wars; knowing the distinction protects your professional identity.

slides.title: Six values that give the specialty its character

cards.title: Wellness & prevention
cards.text: Strengthen communities and prevent harm, not only repair damage.

cards.title: Strengths & resilience
cards.text: Hunt for resources and capacities, not merely deficits.

cards.title: Lifespan development
cards.text: Meet the child, the adult and the elder at their own developmental tasks.

cards.title: Multicultural justice
cards.text: Culture, faith, gender and poverty shape distress and help-seeking.

cards.title: Evidence-informed practice
cards.text: Choose what works, keep it brief and focal, and measure the result.

cards.title: Advocacy
cards.text: Sometimes the most therapeutic act is to change the wounding system.

slides.narration: Six values give the specialty its character. Wellness and prevention: we would rather strengthen a community than only repair damage. Strengths and resilience: we hunt for resources, not merely deficits. Development across the lifespan: a twelve-year-old, a forty-year-old and a seventy-year-old face different tasks, and we meet each where they are. Multicultural and social justice commitment: culture, faith, gender and poverty shape distress and help-seeking. Brief, focal, evidence-informed practice: we choose what works, and we measure it. And advocacy: sometimes the most therapeutic act is to change the system that wounds the client.

slides.title: What counseling psychologists actually do

items.text: children, adolescents, students, couples, families, workers and older adults.
Adjustment to change; academic and examination stress; career decision-making; grief; relationship conflict.
Mild to moderate anxiety and depression; trauma reactions; health-related adjustment; early substance-use concerns.

schools and universities, hospitals and clinics, workplaces and employee assistance programmes, rehabilitation centres, faith and community organisations, non-governmental organisations, private and telepractice.
the scope is wide, but it is not unlimited. Width is not the same as licence.

slides.narration: What does the scope of practice look like on the ground? Populations: children, adolescents, students, couples, families, workers and older adults. Concerns: adjustment to change, academic and examination stress, career decision-making, grief, relationship conflict, mild to moderate anxiety and depression, trauma reactions, health-related adjustment, and substance-use concerns at an early stage. Settings: schools and universities, hospitals and clinics, workplaces and employee assistance programmes, rehabilitation centres, faith and community organisations, non-governmental organisations, and private or telepractice. Wide, yes. Unlimited, no. And that brings us to limits.

slides.title: Where competence ends and referral begins

items.text: you meet psychosis or severe mood disorder with risk; when medical causes may explain the presentation; when medication review is needed; when forensic or custody questions arise; when the problem exceeds your training.
your own values, history or relationship with the client compromise your objectivity.
counseling psychologists work inside multidisciplinary teams; a warm referral letter is part of the intervention.
if you are unsure whether a case is yours, supervision exists precisely for that question.

callout.label: Rule of thumb:
callout.text: when in doubt, consult your supervisor before you proceed, and document the consultation as part of good practice.

slides.narration: Competence has edges, and naming them is a professional act, not a confession of weakness. Refer onward when you meet psychosis or severe mood disorder with risk; when medical causes may explain the presentation; when the client needs medication review; when forensic or custody questions arise; when the problem exceeds your training, such as specialist eating-disorder or addiction treatment; and whenever your own values or relationship with the client compromise objectivity. Equally, refer in: counseling psychologists work inside multidisciplinary teams, and a warm referral letter is part of the intervention. If you ever feel unsure whether a case is yours, supervision exists precisely for that question.

slides.title: The scientist-practitioner-advocate identity
slides.lede: As scientist you consume and produce evidence. As practitioner you translate it into skilful, humane action. As advocate you change the conditions that manufacture suffering.
slides.narration: So who are you becoming? The classic answer is the scientist, practitioner, and, in newer formulations, the advocate. As scientist you consume and produce evidence: you read outcome research, you measure your own results, you stay humble before data. As practitioner you translate that evidence into skilful, timely, humane action with a real person in front of you. As advocate you notice that some suffering is manufactured by unjust systems, and you act to change conditions, in schools, workplaces and policy. The gold centre of this triangle is you: the integrated counseling psychologist, holding all three roles without letting any one of them dominate.

slides.title: Counseling as science and as art

left.title: The science
items: Theory, technique and treatment sequencing
Measurement, outcome research and fidelity
Hypothesis-testing in every case formulation
Accountability to clients and to the profession

right.title: The art
items: Timing: knowing when to be silent and when to speak
Presence, warmth and the disciplined use of self
Language, metaphor and cultural fluency
Courage to challenge at the right moment

slides.narration: Is counseling an art or a science? The honest answer is both, and the tension is creative. The science side gives you theory, technique, measurement and research evidence: what to do, in what order, with what expected effect. The art side gives you timing, presence, language and intuition: knowing when to be silent, when to challenge, when a metaphor will land where a lecture would bounce off. Science without art is mechanical and cold; art without science is charming but unaccountable. Our discipline asks you to be rigorous enough to be trusted and human enough to be helpful.

slides.title: The person of the counselor

items.text: and honesty about your own wounds; the examined life is a clinical tool.
respect that the client can feel, not merely read in a code of ethics.
the capacity to tolerate another's pain without collapsing or fleeing.
culture, faith, gender and class that are not your own.
ethics practised in private, where no one is watching.
open a reflective journal this week; one page after every skills practice.

slides.narration: Finally this week, a preview of the person of the counselor. Technical skill will not carry you if the person behind the skill is unexamined. The qualities we will cultivate across this programme include self-awareness and honesty about your own wounds; warmth, respect and genuineness; emotional stability and the capacity to tolerate another's pain without collapsing or fleeing; openness to culture and difference; courage to be challenged and to change; and a disciplined ethical conscience. Start a reflective journal now, this week. One page after every skills practice. By week fifteen you will see a counselor forming in those pages.

slides.title: Week 1 in review
items: Counseling psychology applies psychological science to improve functioning and wellbeing across the lifespan.
It sits between guidance and psychotherapy on the helping continuum, distinguished by focus, depth, duration and training.
It shares ground with clinical psychology and psychiatry while keeping its own emphasis on strengths, development, prevention and culture.
Its scope is broad but bounded; referral is a professional skill, not a failure.
It is lived through a scientist-practitioner-advocate identity held by an examined person.
slides.narration: Let us gather the week. Counseling psychology applies psychological science to help people improve functioning and wellbeing across the lifespan. It sits between guidance and psychotherapy on the helping continuum, distinguished by focus, depth, duration and training. It shares ground with clinical psychology and psychiatry while keeping its own emphasis on strengths, development, prevention and culture. Its scope is broad but bounded, and referral is a skill, not a failure. And it is lived through a scientist, practitioner, advocate identity held by an examined person.
